name: Memphis postmodern ceramics
summary: Ceramic vessels from the Memphis group of Milan after 1981. They combine plain geometric solids with loud colour and patterns of stripes, dots and terrazzo, and they ignore good taste.

philosophy.core_thesis: A vase is a toy, a totem and a joke at the same time: its form is a stack of simple solids, and its surface is a pattern in loud colour.
design_principles: Build the form from 3 to 5 simple solids: a cone, a sphere, a cylinder, a cube and a ring.
Use 4 or more bright colours on one piece, with black and white as colours too.
Cover the surface with stripes, dots, zigzags or terrazzo flecks in a regular repeat.
Put two patterns on one object, and let them clash.
Make the glaze flat and glossy, so that the form and the colour read as one graphic.
Name each piece after a place or a myth, and sign it with the name of the designer.
Print the pattern by screen print or decal, and fix it in a second firing at 750 to 850 °C.
Treat the vessel as a statement, not as a holder: a vase may have no opening that works.
anti_patterns: Natural earth colour and a hand-made look
A single tone and a plain surface
Symmetry that is quiet and balanced
Traditional ornament such as scrolls and flowers

form.shape: Vases and bottle vases made of stacked solids, striped jars with a lid, shallow bowls with a stand, and sculptural vessels.
form.profile: A tall, stepped form with a wide cone, a cylinder and a sphere set one on the other; the outline is sharp and geometric.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat, square or round foot that is part of the pattern; the rim is a clean flat circle or a coloured band.
form.proportion: Height 20 to 60 cm; the wall is 4 to 8 mm and the form is often wider at the top than at the base.
rules: Use simple solids and clear steps.
Align the pattern to the edges of each solid.
Make the colours clash at each step.

bodies.rule: Use a white or light body that takes bright colour: an earthenware or a stoneware for strong shapes, and a porcelain for fine pieces. Plastic parts may form a base.

methods: screen printing of patterns on the glazed surface
forming.joins: The solids are cast in separate moulds and joined with slip; the seam falls on a colour edge.
forming.details: Sharp edges between colour fields, a flat even glaze, a printed pattern that is aligned with the solids and a signature mark on the base.

glaze.pattern: Stripes, dots, zigzags and a speckle that looks like terrazzo, in black and white and bright colour, with a flat colour field between them.
glaze.gloss: Flat gloss in most fields, 70 to 95 GU; some fields are matt.
glaze.wear: A printed pattern can wear at the rim; the glossy glaze scratches, and the colours stay bright.

palette.strategy: The loudest primary and secondary colours of the Memphis group, with black and white used as colours.

firing.kiln: A gas tunnel kiln for the body and glaze; a small kiln for the decals and the lustre.
processes: slip casting and joining of the solids
spraying of the flat colour glazes
decal or screen print firing at 750 to 850 °C
firing.scale: Limited editions of a few hundred or thousand pieces, made by small Italian factories.
firing.signs: Sharp colour edges, a very regular printed pattern and a designer's mark on the base.

pieces.form: Stepped vase of a cone, a cylinder and a ring, in red, blue and yellow
Tall bottle with black and white terrazzo speckle and a pink neck
Striped jar with a sphere as a lid, in four colours
Totem-like vessel of stacked solids, with a zigzag pattern
Shallow bowl on a stand, with dots and a bright rim

positive: terrazzo speckle in black and white
glossy flat glaze, sharp colour edges
studio photograph on a pink backdrop

canonical_works.work: Striped vase with a sphere lid

emotion.target_response: A feeling of play and shock: the viewer sees loud colour and odd stacked shapes and smiles, or laughs, or frowns.

use_cases: a loud postmodern vase or jar
a museum label on Italian ceramics of 1982
avoid_when: the brief needs a quiet, natural object
the brief needs hand-thrown rustic ware
the brief needs a classical profile

modifiers.how: Replace the flat colour and print with a thick lava glaze on a moulded body.
Drop the pattern and the stacked solids; keep one plain form and one matt colour.
